account: It is ten o'clock on day 0, and I have reached the plaza for my scheduled market walk. I have not yet seen evidence of any unusual activity or secret undertaking. Townsfolk 30 says there is no news; Townsfolk 10 and 20 are also here. I saw freight nearby holding an emerald, but that alone suggests nothing unusual. The secretary reported no correspondence or unusual concerns. One thing is puzzling: after I successfully handed the secretary my written appointment book, the secretary still asked to borrow it. That may simply be confusion; I cannot infer a motive. Today's three o'clock appointment is also vague: tea with 'the neighbour' at a dockside cottage on the east bank, without a name or exact address. The secretary says they do not know the host or cottage, and I have asked them to find out. They have followed me toward the plaza carrying a writable book. My remaining appointments are lunch at home at noon, office accounts at one, that tea at three, office at four thirty, and home at seven. I still feel I should learn more about town affairs, but I currently have no reliable account of anything happening behind my back, who might be organizing it, or what it would be for.
